internal_alignment: Decoding RF.1.3(c): know the spelling-sound correspondences for silent-e and common vowel teams (ai, ay, ee, ea, oa, ow); decode regularly spelled one-syllable words. L.1.2(d): spell grade-appropriate words (Page 4 sort: different teams can make the same long sound). RF.1.3(b) on Pages 2 and 5. RF.1.1(a) as a light touch on Page 5 only (capital at the start, period at the end). Printed words throughout: the child reads letters and words, never blends by ear without print (that was Resource 1, Sounds in Words). Final-e first, then vowel teams, per the user's standing refinement. All child-reading words are one-syllable, plus high-frequency words (the, is, in, can, on, I, a). No other ea or ow pronunciations, no digraph teaching (Resource 2), no two-syllable words (Resource 10). Internal record only; no standards codes appear on any child page, and no separate answer key is published for this pack.
pack: Grade 1 Reading: Long Vowels: Final-e and Vowel Teams

pages_detail.activities: Adult models each short/long pair first, short then long: cap, cape. Hear how the vowel changes? The child circles the long-vowel word in each pair. The silent e in the long word is teal.
pages_detail.title: Meet Final-e

pages_detail.activities: Child reads the word and draws a line to the matching picture. Pictures are in mixed order; no picture sits beside its own word.
pages_detail.title: Read and Match: Final-e Words

pages_detail.activities: Adult reads each example first. The child circles the two letters in each word that make one sound. The example words are entirely dark blue; only the large team heading is teal.
pages_detail.title: Meet the Vowel Teams

pages_detail.activities: Child reads each word in the bank and writes it in the column of its long vowel sound. Different teams can make the same long sound.
answers: Long A: rain, sail, play, day
Long E: bee, tree, sea, bean
Long O: boat, soap, snow, blow
pages_detail.title: Sort by the Long Vowel Sound

pages_detail.activities: Child reads the sentence and draws a line to the picture it tells about. Every word is decodable from taught patterns or a high-frequency word. The adult points out the capital at the start and the period at the end.
answers: The cat can see the bee. (cat looking at a bee)
The boat is on the lake. (rowboat on a calm lake)
I play in the rain. (child splashing in a puddle with a toy boat)
The kite is in the tree. (large kite caught in a simple tree)
pages_detail.title: Read the Sentences
